newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BRAZIL AND ITALY COLLIDE IN NORTH-EAST ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL AND ITALY COLLIDE IN NORTH-EAST ENGLAND.

text.p: Brazil and Italy collide in the English premier league on Saturday when Middlesbrough host Chelsea in a possible dress rehearsal for this season's F.A. Cup final.
In the red-shirted corner stand Middlesbrough, whose Brazilian duo Juninho and Emerson are starting to motor.
Bryan Robson's expensively assembled side have won their last three matches, suggesting they could still haul themselves clear of 19th place in the 20-team table.

In the blue corner are Ruud Gullit's Chelsea, inspired this season by the trickery of forward Gianfranco Zola, the midfield creativity of Italian compatriot Roberto Di Matteo and -- when he can shoulder his way into the first team -- the great Gianluca Vialli.
It is the nearest thing England has to offer to a repeat of the 1994 World Cup final.
In normal circumstances, Chelsea's Italian threesome would expect to come up against an old friend at Middlesbrough's swanky Riverside stadium on the north-east coast.

But Vialli's former Juventus team mate Fabrizio Ravanelli is struggling to recover from a hamstring strain picked up in Boro's 2-1 midweek defeat of Blackburn and faces a late fitness test ahead of Saturday's clash.
Ravanelli has scored 26 goals this season and, with Middlesbrough fast running out of games from which to garner points, his absence would be sorely missed.
Middlesbrough's second Italian Gianluca Festa is expected to start and could be given the daunting job of stopping Zola in his tracks.
While Boro's league form has veered from erratic to downright catastrophic this season, their cup record has been impressive.
They have already clinched a place in the League Cup final and only second division Chesterfield stand between them and a second Wembley appearance in the F.A. Cup final.
That could bring them up against Chelsea, who face Wimbledon in the other semifinal.
Chelsea, in fifth place in the league and bidding for a place in Europe, enter the match on the back of their 6-2 victory over Sunderland last weekend and a 1-0 win over Southampton in midweek.

Influential French defender Franck Leboeuf is still out with a thigh strain and first-choice goalkeeper Kevin Hitchcock is nursing an injured shoulder, but wing-back Scott Minto returns from suspension.
Victory over Chelsea would set Middlesbrough up nicely for what could be the most important week of their nerve-jangling season.
On Tuesday they face fellow strugglers Nottingham Forest in what will be a tense league clash.
Then on Wednesday they launch an appeal against a three-point deduction imposed by the Football Association in January after Middlesbrough cancelled a league match at Blackburn.
True to form, Boro have hired one of the biggest and costliest names in the business to pull them out of a sticky situation.

George Carmen QC, one of the most feared defence lawyers in Britain, will try to win back three points for Middlesbrough which, at the end of the season, could mean the difference between premier league survival and the ignominy of first division football.
